subject: Myth & Symbolism
title: Sacred Geometry in Architecture
description: Learn Sacred Geometry in Architecture in one minute.

hook.text: Gothic cathedrals encoded geometric ratios in stone. The builders believed God spoke through proportion.

buildup.text: Islamic mosques use tessellations—repeating geometric patterns—because depicting God is forbidden. Math fills the void.

discovery.text: The vesica piscis—two overlapping circles—appears in Christian, pagan, and Hindu temples. A shared sacred shape.

twist.text: Modern architects abandoned sacred geometry. Function replaced symbolism. Buildings stopped encoding the divine.

climax.text: Sacred architecture assumed geometry was God's language. Every angle and ratio was a theological argument in stone.

punchline.text: The building is a prayer. Read the angles.

quiz.question: Why do Islamic mosques use geometric patterns?
options: Because depicting God is forbidden, so geometry replaces imagery
